angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 452,205 km at 162.25 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1631 +/- 0.0483 mas (same row, RUWE 2.58): 162.25 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.65 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-228 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 452,205 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.71 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-228 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4715 +/- 48 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-228 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-228 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-228.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.663, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, K2-228: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-228 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.25 dex, from Livingston et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-228 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.84881, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2 (Stellar rotation periods from K2 Campaigns 0-18), column Prot: 18.35 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2 (Stellar rotation periods from K2 Campaigns 0-18), column Prot: 18.35 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 102 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43): 18.22 d, the light swinging by 0.24% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
